properties.details_shown: Fog, tar, and gulls; the far piers are rotting. Morning fog still sits on the docks; the party looks for a boat at pier four.

sources.quote: Morning in Gullwick. The fog is still sitting on the docks, gulls everywhere, and you're standing at the end of pier four looking for a boat.

changes.why: Adds the location shown in this scene.

properties.played_as: Whispers as if the water might hear her; avoids eye contact and watches the tide line. Grey braid, salt-stained coat; mends a net on an upturned skiff.

sources.quote: There's a woman sitting on an upturned skiff, mending a net. Grey braid, salt-stained coat. She doesn't look up.
She talks in a whisper, like the water might hear her, and she never once looks you in the eye. She keeps her gaze on the tide line.
Sela, Sella, the dockhands say it both ways.

changes.why: Records the newly encountered NPC and the GM's spelling and portrayal.

properties.role: Tide-reader who offers to row the party to the old chapel
properties.wants: Will row the party by day, never at night.
properties.knows: Says Saltmere flooded the night the bell first rang, forty years ago; her grandmother said the water came up warm. Claims hers is the only boat that goes near the bell water.

sources.quote: Sela Thorn. I read the tides. I'll row you, but not at night. Never at night.
Sella's boat is the only one that goes near the bell water. The others are scared.
Saltmere flooded the same night the bell first rang. Forty years ago. My grandmother said the water came up warm.

changes.why: Records Sela's stated terms and claims without confirming them.

sources.quote: She shrugs and goes back to her net. She says she'll be at pier four tomorrow at first light if you want the ride.

changes.why: Records where the party last encountered Sela.

properties.statement: Sela says Saltmere flooded the night the bell first rang, forty years ago; her grandmother said the floodwater came up warm.

sources.quote: Saltmere flooded the same night the bell first rang. Forty years ago. My grandmother said the water came up warm.

changes.why: Adds a claimed historical link between mine and bell, keeping the grandmother's report attributed.

change.name: How are Saltmere and the drowned bell connected?

properties.what_is_open: Sela says the mine flooded the night the bell first rang, forty years ago. The timing and connection remain unconfirmed.

sources.quote: Saltmere flooded the same night the bell first rang. Forty years ago. My grandmother said the water came up warm.

changes.why: Opens a lead from Sela's account.

properties.details_shown: Up the cliff path, closed for forty years. Entrance is a black mouth in chalk with half-rotted timber framing and a rusted cart on its side. Warm air smells of old candle wax. Thirty paces in, warm black water floods the tunnel; wet hymn-book pages float and cling to the walls. One hymn describes the sea giving back what it takes and bears the pencilled margin inscription "M. Brand".
properties.state: Closed; tunnel flooded thirty paces inside with warm black water.

sources.quote: The Saltmere Mine entrance is a black mouth in the chalk, timber frame half rotted. A rusted cart lies on its side. The air coming out of it is warm and smells like a church, like old candle wax.
About thirty paces in, the tunnel floods. Black water, and it's warm to the touch. Floating on it, stuck to the walls, there are pages. Wet pages from a hymn book.
A hymn about the sea giving back what it takes. And in the margin, in pencil, someone wrote "M. Brand".

changes.why: Adds the mine's observed condition and inscription without assigning authorship.

properties.what_is_open: Sela's claimed flooding date remains unconfirmed. Saltmere contains warm floodwater and hymn-book pages; one bears "M. Brand". Why are the pages there, and how is the mine connected to the bell?

sources.quote: About thirty paces in, the tunnel floods. Black water, and it's warm to the touch. Floating on it, stuck to the walls, there are pages. Wet pages from a hymn book.
A hymn about the sea giving back what it takes. And in the margin, in pencil, someone wrote "M. Brand".

changes.why: Advances the historical lead with direct observations.

properties.what_changed: Mira heard the bell the night she left. Teo identifies the "M. Brand" handwriting on a hymn-book page at Saltmere as his sister's and concludes she was there; authorship and her presence are unconfirmed.

sources.quote: That's Mira. That's my sister's handwriting. She was here.

changes.why: Records Teo's identification as his interpretation, not an established fact about Mira.

change.name: Is Maren involved with the cult or choir?

properties.what_is_open: Vessa suspects Maren is behind events and in the cult; Oren suspects she runs the choir. Neither theory has been confirmed.

sources.quote: Okay, I bet the harbor-master is behind all this. Maren wanted us gone from day one. She's in the cult, I'm calling it.
Yeah, Maren is totally running the choir.

changes.why: Tracks the players' suspicions without changing Maren.

properties.statement: A fisherman says the Kelp Mother pulls children who stand too close to the water down by the ankles; her existence is unconfirmed.

sources.quote: Don't stand that close. The Kelp Mother takes children who stand that close. Pulls them down by the ankles. Everyone knows that.
That's what the fishermen say. They pull their boat up and leave.

changes.why: Records local folklore without creating a creature NPC.

properties.details_shown: Previously described as sunk into the bay with its bell. At low water the roof, bell tower and two broken arches stick out of the bay; seaweed hangs from the stones. At midnight the underwater bell rings twelve times, with humming much louder than two nights before, felt in the teeth. Pale shapes stand in rows on the chapel floor like a congregation, then disappear when the bell stops.

sources.quote: The drowned chapel's roof sticks out of the bay at low water, just the bell tower and two broken arches. Seaweed hangs from the stones.
And then, right at midnight, the bell rings again under the water. Twelve times. And the humming is back, but louder. Much louder than two nights ago. You can feel it in your teeth.
Shapes. Pale shapes, standing on the chapel floor under the water, in rows. Like a congregation. Then the bell stops and they're gone.

changes.why: Adds the chapel's visible details and the witnessed midnight event.

properties.what_is_open: Who or what rings the drowned bell? At midnight it rang twelve times with louder humming; pale shapes stood in rows on the submerged chapel floor and vanished when the bell stopped.

sources.quote: And then, right at midnight, the bell rings again under the water. Twelve times. And the humming is back, but louder. Much louder than two nights ago. You can feel it in your teeth.
Shapes. Pale shapes, standing on the chapel floor under the water, in rows. Like a congregation. Then the bell stops and they're gone.

changes.why: Advances the bell mystery with a new witnessed manifestation.

sources.quote: That's the choir clock at three of six.

changes.why: Uses the GM's explicit clock value; visibility and total segments stay as recorded.

properties.details_shown: Tavern by the docks, with a fire going and the smell of tar and fish stew.

sources.quote: You end up back at the Tarred Gull, the tavern by the docks. Fire going, it smells of tar and fish stew.

changes.why: Records the newly shown tavern.

properties.next_step: The party plans for Sela to row them out tomorrow at first light and to dive to the chapel at low tide during the day.

sources.quote: At low tide, during the day. Not at night, Sela was right about that.
So tomorrow, first light, Sela rows us out and we dive to the chapel at low tide. I'll buy rope and a second lantern tonight.
Agreed. Tomorrow we dive.

changes.why: Records the agreed intended next step without treating the dive as completed.

properties.what_changed: Mira heard the bell the night she left. Teo identifies Saltmere's "M. Brand" handwriting as Mira's, unconfirmed, and links the hymn book to the chapel. He plans to follow the lead by diving to the chapel with the party tomorrow at first light, at low tide.

sources.quote: Okay, plan. Mira wrote in that hymn book. The chapel is where the hymns came from. We go down to the chapel.
Agreed. Tomorrow we dive.

changes.why: Records Teo's plan and interpretation on his existing goal.

properties.played_as: Huge, red-bearded; laughs at his own jokes and wipes the same mug while talking. Offers stew without being asked.

sources.quote: The innkeeper, Bram, sets down three bowls of stew without being asked.
Bram is huge, red beard, laughs at his own jokes, and he wipes the same mug the whole time he talks to you.

changes.why: Records the newly encountered innkeeper and the GM's portrayal.

properties.knows: Says he has known Maren for thirty years; describes her as sharp-tongued and good-hearted, and says she lost a brother to the bay.

sources.quote: Maren? Thirty years I've known her. Sharp tongue. Good heart. She lost a brother to that bay.

changes.why: Records Bram's account without confirming Maren's history.
